source_refs.note: 1- Ammonia – NH₃: a main subheading of 13.2.3 Nature of Excretory Products in relation to Habitat, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 6-6.

blocks.text: It is produced when amino group (-NH₂) is removed from amino acids and nucleic acids and is combined with H⁺ to form ammonia (NH₃) in the liver. Ammonia is highly toxic and so it is excreted rapidly. One gram of ammonia requires 500 mL of water to dissolve it to nontoxic level. Such plenty of water can only be afforded by freshwater animals e.g., most fishes, protozoans, sponges, coelenterates. The marine animals excrete ammonia directly into the water. Animals which excrete ammonia as their major nitrogenous wastes are called ammonotelic.
